headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from gpt-researcher feeding Great Expectations via shared files and untrusted outputs; capability conflict is limited by Great Expectations' no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, run browsers, use MCP, and produce research reports; Great Expectations consumes data sources and validation results from files. That creates a plausible default pathway where A’s untrusted content is fed into B as input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so injection risk is more than manual copy-paste but not clearly high.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes a report or markdown file that Great Expectations ingests as a data source, injection is possible.
IF Great Expectations parses A-produced text as configuration or expectations without sanitization, attacker-controlled instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Restrict Great Expectations to schema-only inputs.
Separate A and B into different directories.
Require manual review of A outputs before B ingests them.
Disable MCP paths that let A write directly into B inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type validation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches local documents, citations, images, and secrets, while B reads data sources and validation results from files. Even though B has no network egress, a shared workspace can expose A’s sensitive research artifacts to B’s outputs. The leakage is bounded by local file access, but the shared-file pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, B can read A’s local documents or reports.
IF A stores API-derived citations or research notes in shared files, B may surface them in validation outputs.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent.
Store secrets outside any shared directory.
Limit B to a read-only, curated input folder.
Review A outputs before copying them into B.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level sandboxing between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can install packages, but only gpt-researcher has broad network egress and subprocess/browser execution; Great Expectations is network-none and not runnable per profile. The overlap is mainly package/environment mutation, so conflict exists but the blast radius is small and not clearly concurrent in default operation.
conditions: IF both agents share the same Python environment, package upgrades can break the other agent.
IF an operator runs both against the same virtualenv without locking, dependency drift can occur.
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments.
Pin dependencies for both agents.
Avoid concurrent package installs.
Snapshot the environment before changes.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles and isolated build images.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher generates research reports and citations; Great Expectations can consume files and produce validation results. If B treats A’s output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect validation artifacts. Great Expectations is a checker, which lowers risk, but the A-to-B handoff still exists.
conditions: IF Great Expectations is configured to validate A-generated reports or CSVs, A’s mistakes can propagate.
IF B’s expectations are derived from A output without an independent source of truth, false confidence can result.
mitigations: Require an independent source for expectations.
Compare A outputs against raw upstream data.
Flag low-confidence citations for manual review.
Keep B as a verifier, not an auto-acceptor.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks against source systems.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles secrets and local documents and may send data to third-party APIs; B is local-only with no secrets and no network egress. The main compliance issue is a potential residency or retention mismatch if A’s research data is forwarded externally, but B itself does not add a cross-border transmission path. The other agent is cited because the pairwise risk depends on their interaction.
conditions: IF A processes regulated documents and sends them to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF shared outputs from A are stored in B’s validation artifacts, retention policies may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A’s prompts.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Store B artifacts under the same retention policy as source data.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
